300H: Evac+Chair Lightweight Evacuation Stair Chair
Product URL: https://www.anchortex.com/products/evac-chair-300h-evacuation-stair-chair
Manufacturer page: https://www.evac-chair.com/evacuation-chairs/evacchair-300h/
Spec sheets: 300H data sheet, Evac+Chair range brochure
Keywords (Ricky's sheet): Primary: evacuation stair chair (70/mo, KD4). Secondary: evac chair 300h (40, KD1), emergency evacuation chair for stairs (60). Ricky's note: original standard model; the model-number term (evac chair 300h) goes in the title and body.
Recommended H1 and Subtitle
H1: Evac+Chair Lightweight Evacuation Stair Chair with Dual-Position Seat – 300H
Current H1: Evac+Chair 300H Evacuation Stair Chair
Subtitle: 19 lb Evacuation Stair Chair with a 400 lb Capacity and a Flat or Hammock Seat for One-Person Emergency Evacuation Down the Stairs
Current subtitle: Evac+Chair 300H Stairway Evacuation Chair
Revised Product Description
Headings marked [H2] should be set as H2 on the page.
The Evac+Chair 300H is the original Evac+Chair evacuation stair chair: a lightweight, folding chair that lets one operator move a person with limited mobility safely down the stairs in an emergency. When a fire, tornado, or power outage means the elevators cannot be used, the 300H gets people who cannot manage the stairs on their own out of the building.
As an emergency evacuation chair for stairs, it is built to be simple: self-braking Evac+Track friction tracks control the speed of descent, so a small operator can move a passenger up to three times their size with no heavy lifting. At only 19 lbs, it folds flat for wall mounted storage near the stairwell and opens in seconds.
Operation: One operator for downward evacuation, with no heavy lifting
Tracks: Self-braking, reinforced Evac+Track friction tracks control the speed of descent
Dual Position Seat: Flat seat with zipped side panels, or release the panels and fasten them underneath for a hammock seat, chosen each time
Head Restraint: Adjustable patient head restraint limits movement and secures the passenger
Safety Belts: Quick-release head, chest, and thigh belts, with an over-thigh restraint in both seat positions
Handle: Ergonomic adjustable handle for easy deployment and compact storage
Wheels: Heavy duty wheels for uneven ground, with lockable rear wheels to keep the chair stationary
Visibility: Reflective decals for poor visibility
Finish: Blue powder coated textured frame with a fire retardant yellow seat
Weight Capacity: 400 lbs
Weight: 19 lbs
Folded Size: 20”W×8”D×41”H
Storage: Folds for compact storage and is wall mountable
Certifications: FDA registered
Compliance: Exceeds fire safety requirements and emergency response guidelines established to support the Americans with Disabilities Act
Includes: 3 passenger safety belts (head, chest, thigh), photoluminescent signage, wall mounting brackets, dust cover, and user guide
Warranty: Lifetime manufacturer’s warranty
Design: Designed in the United States
Available Models and Options
300H – Evacuation Stair Chair: Dual-position seat, one-person operation, 400 lb capacity, 19 lbs
[H2] Applications
The 300H suits any building with stairs where people with limited mobility, injuries, or health conditions may need help getting out in an emergency.
Typical applications include:
Offices, high-rise buildings, and hotels
Schools, colleges, and universities
Hospitals, clinics, senior living, and care facilities
Government buildings and public venues, as part of an emergency evacuation plan
Explore Anchortex's Evacuation Chairs and Stretchers collection for more evacuation equipment.
[H2] Frequently Asked Questions
How many people does it take to use the Evac+Chair 300H?
One. The 300H is designed for single person operation. The operator guides the chair down the stairs on its friction tracks, which control the speed of descent.
Can the 300H go up the stairs?
No. The 300H is an evacuation stair chair for going down the stairs. For upward evacuation, Evac+Chair makes the 600H, which has carry handles, and the battery powered Power 800 and Power 900 stair climbing chairs.
What is the dual-position seat?
The seat can be used flat, with zipped side panels, or as a hammock seat by releasing the side panels and fastening them underneath. The over-thigh quick-release restraint works in both positions.
Where should an emergency evacuation chair for stairs be stored?
Mount it on the wall near the stairwell, using the wall mounting brackets, dust cover, and photoluminescent sign that come with the 300H, so it is easy to find and ready to use. Evac+Chair recommends regular training for operators, ideally during fire drills.
[H2] About Evac+Chair Evacuation Chairs
Evac+Chair makes stair evacuation chairs, powered stair chairs, evacuation sleds, and accessories for moving people with limited mobility on stairs, in an emergency or every day.
The Evac+Chair line includes:
Emergency evacuation chairs: The 300H, 400H, 600H, and 750H stair evacuation chairs for controlled travel down the stairs
Powered stair climbing chairs: The battery powered Power 800 and Power 900 for going up and down the stairs
Stair transport seat: The IBEX 700H Tran-Seat for two-person transport up and down the stairs
Evacuation sleds and mats: The Evac+Sled, Ulti-Mat, and Evac+Sheet rescue sheet
Accessories: Comfy Seat, transfer seat, storage cabinets, anti-theft alarms, and the iEvac smoke and fire escape hood
[H2] About Evac+Chair
Evac+Chair has made stairway evacuation chairs since 1982, and its chairs were designed in the United States. Explore the full line of Evac+Chair evacuation chairs at Anchortex.

Notes and Questions
Keywords: the primary keyword "evacuation stair chair" is in the H1, subtitle, first sentence, an FAQ answer, the meta title, and the meta description. As Ricky noted, the model-number term "evac chair 300h" is covered by "Evac+Chair 300H" in the meta title, the first sentence, and the FAQs. The secondary keyword "emergency evacuation chair for stairs" is in the second intro paragraph and an FAQ question. "Stair evacuation chair" and "emergency evacuation chair" stay on the collection page (Ricky), so they are not used as main terms here.
Research: the search results for "evacuation stair chair" are product and category pages (Stryker, Grainger, Global Industrial, Staples). Retailers put the capacity in the product name (for example "Evacuation Stair Chair, 400 lbs. Capacity"), so I put the 19 lb weight and 400 lb capacity in the subtitle. The questions buyers ask most (how many operators, up or down the stairs, storage, training) are answered in the FAQs.
Specs: weight, capacity, folded size, and warranty are the same on the Evac+Chair web page, the 300H data sheet, the range brochure, and our current page.
Instructional DVD: on the data sheet, but not on the Evac+Chair web page or our page. I left it out, as you decided for the 600H and 700H.
Left out: "the only evacuation chair on the market with a dual position seat" (the 600H also has one), "World's No.1," and "Successful in saving lives in 9/11."
Duplicate content: our current description is the Evac+Chair text word for word, and many other stores use the same text. The new copy is fully rewritten.
Images: the 3 current images are kept (chair with numbered features, flat seat, and hammock seat). Evac+Chair also has a photo of the 300H in use on a stairwell (1920×1080). Would you like me to add it as "Evac-Chair-300H-Evacuation-Stair-Chair-Stairwell-View.jpg"?
Shipping weight: the variant is set to 200 lbs; the chair weighs 19 lbs. Is 200 lbs a placeholder, as on the Power 900?
Price: $1,595 with compare-at $2,127 (75%, like the other Evac+Chair pages). No change made.
Current meta description is the general GSA pricing line. Per your note on the other tabs, GSA is not mentioned in the description.
